rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rights statement and fee cap disclosure
rules.requirement: When charging a fee to purchase a consumer credit report or process an application, the owner must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under state law, in the application or a separate disclosure before receiving the fee.
rules.quoted_span: the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
rules.key_value: Disclosure of fee rights and state cap ($68.96 for 2026)
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in document.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on non-refundable application fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners cannot charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees for a roommate departure or for adding or replacing a roommate.
rules.quoted_span: cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part

rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap and rules
rules.requirement: Screening fees are capped (2026 maximum $68.96 per Berkeley Rent Board). Landlords must give a receipt, itemized expenses, a copy of the credit report, and refund unused fees; no fee if no unit is available; must accept a reusable screening report.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in document.
rules.conflict_note: The $68.96 figure is from the Berkeley page; no single official state dollar figure for 2026 is confirmed.

parsed.doc_summary: Berkeley Rent Board page on tenant screening and application fees: state fee cap and refund rules (Civ. Code § 1950.6), plus Berkeley BMC ch. 13.78 disclosure and a ban on non-refundable renewal fees.
